chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn al-Hakam, who said: I heard Safwan saying:

I said to Al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, a man from your mawali (clients/followers) ordered me to ask you about a matter; he feared you and felt shy from you to ask you himself.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is it?'

I said: 'The man has intercourse with his wife from behind (in her rear).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, that is permissible for him.' I said: 'And do you do that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, we do not do that.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the Eighth Imam, Ali ibn Musa)
key_terms.دُبُرِهَا: Her rear (referring to the dorsal position in intercourse)
key_terms.مَوَالِيكَ: Your mawali (clients, followers, or freed slaves associated with the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a husband to have intercourse with his wife from behind according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that while intercourse from behind is generally permissible (halal) for men, the Ahl al-Bayt abstain from it as a mark of distinction and refined etiquette (adab). The distinction between general permissibility and the specific practice of the Imams highlights the Shia emphasis on following the Prophet's household as the ideal model of conduct, even in matters where the ruling is not strictly prohibitive.
